title: Direct identifiability from rich biometric and location telemetry shared by the wearer
description: By providing continuous heart-rate, step-count, GPS-position, and timestamp data to the wearable device, the wearer shares data that can directly or indirectly identify them. Persistent location traces and physiological patterns can single out a person even without an explicit name.
assumptions: The device can associate incoming telemetry with a persistent device/user context.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on generic LINDDUN identifiability categorization; exact subnode may differ in the project taxonomy.

title: Linkability of telemetry records over time in transit
description: The flow contains repeated sensor telemetry plus timestamps and GPS coordinates. Even if explicit identifiers are absent, the combination enables linking multiple observations to the same wearer across time, revealing routines and habits.
assumptions: Telemetry is transmitted in a form where repeated records can be correlated by stable attributes, timing, or communication metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary; this is a best-fit generic linkability node.

title: Detectability of wearer activity and presence from transmission patterns
description: Continuous telemetry transmission can make it observable that a person is wearing and actively using the device. Communication timing, frequency, and payload characteristics may reveal when the wearer is moving, exercising, or present at certain places.
assumptions: An observer can access network or local radio metadata associated with the telemetry flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort generic detectability node; exact subnode not provided in retrieved context.

title: Linkability through aggregation of multiple sensor modalities at the wearable device
description: On receipt, the wearable device can combine heart rate, steps, GPS, and timestamps into a persistent profile, making it easy to link separate events and sessions to the same wearer.
assumptions: The device stores or otherwise correlates telemetry across time under a stable device or user context.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate.

title: Identification of the wearer by the receiving device
description: The wearable device may identify the wearer from unique movement patterns, habitual routes, or biometric characteristics contained in the telemetry, even if the flow lacks an explicit real-world identifier.
assumptions: The device software maintains user profiles or can infer identity from behavioral/biometric uniqueness.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate; applicability depends on whether the device distinguishes among possible users.

title: Inference of sensitive activities and states by the wearable device
description: By processing incoming telemetry, the device can detect sensitive facts such as sleep/wake cycles, exercise routines, visits to locations, or possible health conditions. This exceeds mere receipt of raw data and creates privacy-relevant observability of the wearer’s behavior.
assumptions: The device analyzes or stores telemetry rather than treating it as ephemeral raw input.
uncertainty_note: This is framed as detectability/inference at the destination; some methodologies might classify parts of this under disclosure instead.

title: Unawareness of continuous collection and downstream privacy implications
description: The wearable device may collect and process telemetry continuously in ways the wearer does not fully understand, including the granularity of GPS/timestamp capture and the extent to which behavior and health patterns can be inferred.
assumptions: User notices or consent mechanisms are limited, unclear, or not continuously salient during passive collection.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode is approximate; this depends on the actual transparency and UX of the device.

title: Potential non-compliance from collecting more telemetry than necessary
description: Continuous capture of GPS position, timestamps, heart rate, and step counts may exceed what is necessary for a given function if data minimization, purpose limitation, retention limits, or valid consent are not properly implemented at the device.
assumptions: Not all listed telemetry is strictly necessary for every device function, or legal basis/retention controls are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Compliance assessment is context-dependent; exact legal non-compliance cannot be concluded from the flow alone.

title: Excessive disclosure of fine-grained activity and location data by the wearable
description: The wearable shares exercise sessions, GPS traces, device identifier, and timestamps with the companion app in one sync flow. If all fields are not strictly necessary for the app feature being invoked, the device causes avoidable disclosure of personal data, especially sensitive movement/location history and persistent identifiers.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app does not always need raw GPS traces, persistent device id, and exact timestamps for every sync, or could operate with reduced precision/minimized fields.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement for explicit/minimization-related disclosure; retrieved context confirms Dd applicability but not the exact subnode.

title: Identification via persistent device identifier and unique mobility patterns in transit
description: The flow contains a device id and GPS traces with timestamps. Even if the user is not named, these data can identify a specific individual because persistent identifiers and distinctive location trajectories are often uniquely attributable.
assumptions: Assumes the sync payload or transport metadata exposes the device id and/or sufficiently detailed traces to parties able to observe or process the flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact I subnode is best-judgement; identification risk is strongly supported by the nature of the data.

title: Linkability of multiple sync events and datasets through stable identifiers and timestamps
description: Repeated syncs carrying the same device id plus timestamps allow records from different sessions to be linked together. GPS traces further enable linking with other datasets containing co-located or time-correlated observations, building a longitudinal profile of the user.
assumptions: Assumes the identifier is stable across syncs or the trajectory/timing data remain sufficiently consistent to correlate events.
uncertainty_note: Exact L subnode is best-judgement; applicability is high given stable identifiers and temporal/location data.

title: Detectability of user activity from sync timing and traffic characteristics
description: Even without reading payload contents, the existence, timing, size, and frequency of sync traffic can reveal when the user exercised, traveled, or used the wearable. This makes private behavior detectable from the data flow's metadata.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can see network or local communication metadata such as sync occurrence, packet sizes, or timing.
uncertainty_note: Exact D subnode is best-judgement; threat is based on metadata observability rather than payload inspection.

title: Secondary use of synced sensor and location data by the companion app
description: Once received, the companion app may use exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, and timestamps for purposes beyond core synchronization, such as analytics, profiling, personalization, or sharing onward. Such processing can exceed the user's reasonable expectations for the original collection purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the app has capabilities or business incentives to repurpose received data beyond immediate device-companion functionality.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subnode is best-judgement; the threat depends on downstream app behavior not fully specified in the flow description.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for collection of detailed location and activity data in the app
description: The companion app may receive detailed GPS traces, timestamps, and device identifiers without the user being clearly informed of the granularity, frequency, retention, or purposes of this sync. If so, the receipt and subsequent processing occur without valid, specific, and informed consent or another clear legal basis.
assumptions: Assumes consent/notice is handled by the app and may be incomplete for this sync flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nc subnode is best-judgement; applicability depends on the app's notice/consent design, which is not described.

title: User may be unaware of the privacy implications of entering sensitive health-related data
description: The wearer manually shares calorie intake, meal details, and weight in the app without fully understanding what personal data is being disclosed, how long it will be retained, who may access it, or what secondary uses may follow. This creates unawareness at the moment of sharing.

title: Companion app can detect sensitive health and lifestyle attributes from logged entries
description: On receipt of calorie intake, meals, and weight entries, the companion app can infer sensitive attributes such as dieting behavior, possible medical conditions, religious or cultural dietary patterns, pregnancy-related changes, or eating-disorder indicators. The privacy threat arises from the destination processing these data into sensitive knowledge about the user.

title: Companion app can link nutrition and weight logs to the identified wearer profile
description: Because the entries are submitted through the user's companion app account/device context, the destination can associate meal, calorie, and weight logs with the same wearer over time and combine them with other app data. This enables linkability of multiple records and behaviors to one person.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate; the retrieved context only established that linkability is applicable for ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Companion app can identify the wearer from the submitted logs and account context
description: Even if individual food or weight entries seem innocuous, when received in the authenticated app context they are directly attributable to the wearer, making the data identifiable at the destination.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is approximate; identification clearly applies, but the exact subtree citation was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Companion app may process health-related logs without a valid legal basis or compatible purpose
description: Calorie intake, meal details, and weight are health-related or highly sensitive lifestyle data in many contexts. If the app collects or further processes these entries without a clearly established legal basis, explicit consent where required, or purpose compatibility, the receipt and processing of this flow may be non-compliant.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on jurisdiction, controller role, and exact purposes disclosed to the user.

title: App writes more health data than necessary to the store
description: The mobile app may disclose excessive personal health data to the health log store by writing detailed calorie intake, weight history, and exercise-session records beyond what is strictly necessary for the app's stated purpose. This creates avoidable disclosure at the moment of sharing from the source process.

title: Health-log contents could be exposed in transit to the data store
description: The flow carries sensitive health-related personal data. If the write operation is insufficiently protected in transit, the contents or revealing metadata of the logs could be disclosed while moving from the app to the health log store.
assumptions: Assumes the communication path or API call could be observed by an unauthorized party due to missing or weak transport protection.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; the applicability of in-transit disclosure depends on deployment and transport protections.

title: Repeated health-log uploads may enable linkage of records to the same user
description: Even if individual log entries are not directly identifying on their own, repeated writes of weight history, calorie intake, and exercise sessions over the same flow can allow records to be linked together as belonging to the same person or device through stable identifiers, account tokens, timestamps, or consistent behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the flow includes stable identifiers or metadata, or that the pattern of submissions is sufficiently distinctive.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort; linkage may arise from metadata and behavioral consistency rather than explicit identifiers.

title: Health-log metadata may identify the user
description: The transmitted health logs and accompanying metadata such as account ID, device ID, session token, or precise timestamps may directly or indirectly identify the individual whose health data is being stored.

uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; identification may be direct or indirect depending on payload design.

title: Store may retain overly detailed or long-lived health logs

uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort and may differ in another LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Users may be unaware that detailed health histories are stored
description: The destination datastore's receipt and storage of calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions may be insufficiently transparent to users, especially if the app does not clearly communicate what is stored, at what granularity, and for how long.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or in-app explanations do not clearly describe storage practices for these logs.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; this threat depends on the surrounding notice and transparency design.

title: Storage of health logs may exceed or diverge from user consent
description: The health log store may receive and keep sensitive health-related data in ways not covered by the user's consent or choice settings, for example storing categories, detail levels, or retention periods beyond what the user agreed to.
assumptions: Assumes consent or preference controls exist or are expected for health-data storage, and that actual storage behavior may not align with them.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; applicability depends on whether consent is the chosen legal basis and how user choices are implemented.

title: Excessive collection and storage of precise location traces
description: The mobile app writes GPS traces with timestamps to the location history store. Precise, timestamped location history is highly sensitive personal data; collecting and persisting full traces may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the app's purpose if granularity, frequency, or retention are not minimized.
assumptions: Assumes the app's purpose could be fulfilled with less precise, less frequent, aggregated, or shorter-retained location data.

title: Identification through precise location-and-time data in transit
description: The data flow carries GPS coordinates together with timestamps. Even without explicit identifiers, such spatiotemporal traces can identify a person by linking home/work patterns or unique movement trajectories to a real-world individual.

uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode is inferred from standard LINDDUN identification threats for quasi-identifiers and unique patterns.

title: Linkability of multiple app events via recurring location traces
description: Repeated uploads of timestamped GPS traces on this flow can be linked together to the same user, device, or routine. The recurring pattern of locations and times enables correlation across sessions and with other datasets.

uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is best-judgement for linkability from repeated observations.

title: Detectability of sensitive presence and routines from stored location history
description: Once received and stored, the location history store can reveal whether a person was present at sensitive places or followed particular routines. Even if full identity is not immediately known, the existence of records for specific times and places may allow an observer or internal actor to detect a user's visits, habits, or absences.
assumptions: Assumes the store can be queried, indexed, or otherwise inspected by parties beyond the data subject, including administrators or analytics components.
uncertainty_note: Subnode id is inferred from generic detectability threats; exact numbering may vary.

title: Secondary use of stored location history beyond the user's expectations
description: The destination store enables later analysis of historical movement data for profiling, analytics, targeted advertising, law-enforcement requests, or other purposes beyond the immediate app function. Such downstream processing may be unexpected by users when they share location data through the app.
assumptions: Assumes governance and purpose limitation controls are absent or weak, allowing reuse of stored traces.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is best-judgement for use of data beyond user expectations/purpose limitation.

title: Insufficient consent or legal basis for persistent location-history storage
description: Persistently storing timestamped GPS traces may require explicit, informed consent or another valid legal basis, especially given the sensitivity of location history. If the store retains these traces without sufficiently specific notice, choice, or withdrawal mechanisms, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes the system operates in a jurisdiction where location history is regulated personal data and that consent/legal-basis management may be inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode id is inferred from generic non-compliance/consent-lawfulness threats.

title: Excessive disclosure of longitudinal health logs to analytics
description: The data store discloses calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions to the analytics service. Because these are sensitive health-related and behavioral data, sharing the full longitudinal history may exceed what is strictly necessary for the stated health-condition analysis, creating avoidable disclosure through over-broad retrieval.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics task could be performed with a reduced time window, aggregation, or fewer attributes than the full cross-session log history.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality structure; exact subnode label may vary by version.

description: This flow carries longitudinal records spanning multiple sessions to one analytics service. Even if direct identifiers are minimized, the repeated transfer of stable health and activity patterns can allow records from different sessions to be linked to the same individual, enabling construction of a persistent profile.
assumptions: Assumes records contain stable pseudonyms, account references, timestamps, or distinctive behavioral patterns sufficient to correlate sessions.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; threat applicability is strong because the flow is explicitly cross-session and longitudinal.

title: Identifiability from unique combinations of health and activity attributes in transit
description: Calorie, weight, and exercise logs can form a distinctive combination, especially when combined with timestamps or session metadata on the flow. This may allow the subject to be singled out or re-identified from the transmitted dataset even if obvious identifiers are absent.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted records include enough granularity (e.g., exact weight values, detailed exercise events, dates) to make some users unique.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement and may not exactly match the local threat-tree numbering.

description: Upon receipt, the analytics service performs health-condition analysis over longitudinal logs. This processing can reveal new sensitive information, such as suspected conditions, risk scores, or lifestyle patterns, increasing disclosure beyond the raw data originally recorded.
assumptions: Assumes analysis outputs, intermediate features, or stored results are accessible to components, staff, or downstream uses beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Subnode id is approximate; the core threat is disclosure through derived/inferred sensitive data at the destination.

title: Secondary use of health logs for broader analytics than users expect

uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; applicability depends on what users were told about this analytics purpose.

title: Processing of sensitive health data without a valid legal basis or explicit consent
description: Health-condition analysis over calorie, weight, and exercise logs involves special-category or highly sensitive personal data in many jurisdictions. If the analytics service performs this processing without an appropriate legal basis, explicit consent where required, or equivalent justification, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.

description: The location history store may disclose more raw location history than is strictly necessary when answering analytics queries. Because the stated purpose is deriving daily routine and movement patterns across sessions, sharing full cross-session histories can expose highly sensitive movement traces beyond what is needed for a specific analytic task, violating data minimization.
assumptions: DS2 returns detailed historical location records rather than only aggregated or purpose-limited subsets.

description: The analytics service links location history across sessions to derive routines and movement patterns. This enables correlation of records that may otherwise be separate in time or context, creating a persistent profile of the same individual and increasing the ability to connect activities across sessions.
assumptions: Records in DS2 can be associated with the same person, device, or stable pseudonym across sessions.

title: Inference of identity or unique household/workplace from movement patterns
description: By analyzing longitudinal location history, the analytics service may infer a person's identity or uniquely identify them indirectly through recurring home/work locations, commute patterns, or visits to distinctive places, even if direct identifiers are absent from the queried data.
assumptions: Location traces are sufficiently granular and persistent to single out individuals or households.

title: Inference of sensitive habits and routines from historical locations
description: The destination process derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history. These patterns can reveal sensitive personal information such as home address, workplace, religious practice, medical visits, political activity, social relationships, or other private habits that were not explicitly provided for this purpose.

description: Using stored location history across sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns may exceed the purpose originally understood by the data subject, especially if the history was collected for operational or service-delivery reasons rather than longitudinal behavioral analytics. This creates an unawareness threat about how personal data is analyzed and for what purposes.
assumptions: Users were not clearly informed that cross-session location histories would be mined for routine and movement-pattern analytics.
